title: Dependence and Model Selection in LLP: The Problem of Variants

problem.claim: Learning from Label Proportions learns item-labeling hypotheses using only label proportions for predefined bags.

gap.claim: Although algorithmic approaches exist for LLP, little work has addressed model selection, and straightforward extensions are complicated by the lack of item labels.

contributions.claim: The paper formalizes the dependence structure between bags, items, and labels and shows how it affects model selection for LLP.
The paper develops improved methods of model selection for LLP based on consideration of the dependence structure.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their model-selection methods outperform the state of the art across a wide range of datasets and LLP algorithms.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLP is an important problem with practical applications and uses bag-level label proportions instead of item labels.
Model selection for LLP has received little attention and cannot be addressed straightforwardly because item labels are unavailable.
The paper argues that model selection must account for dependence among bags, items, and labels.
The paper formalizes the dependence structure and explains its effect on model selection.
The resulting model-selection methods are reported to outperform the state of the art across diverse datasets and LLP algorithms.

source_observation.claim: Model selection in LLP is affected by dependence among bags, items, and labels.

interpretation.claim: Model-selection procedures for weakly supervised settings should represent and account for relevant dependence structures.

application.claim: When selecting models from aggregate-label data, incorporate the relationships among groups, instances, and labels into the selection procedure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this lesson applies beyond LLP or to settings with different dependence structures.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal dependence structure.
The abstract does not identify the proposed model-selection algorithms.
The abstract does not provide dataset names, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
